draft.title: The Argand plane
card: A complex number z = a + bi has a real part a and an imaginary part b. Both a and b are ordinary real numbers.
The Argand plane shows complex numbers as points. The horizontal axis is the real axis. The vertical axis is the imaginary axis.
To plot z = a + bi, go a units along the real axis and b units up the imaginary axis. This gives the point (a, b).
Example: 3 − 2i has real part 3 and imaginary part −2. It is plotted at (3, −2), which is 3 right and 2 down from the origin.
draft.remember: Real part goes across, imaginary part goes up: a + bi is the point (a, b).

a.q: At which point is the complex number −4 + 5i plotted on the Argand plane?
a.why: The real part −4 gives the horizontal position and the imaginary part 5 gives the vertical position, so the point is (−4, 5). (5, −4) swaps the axes. The i is not part of the coordinate, because the imaginary part is the number 5.
a.clue: Real part first, then the number in front of i.

b.q: Zara plots the complex number 2i − 6 on an Argand plane. Where does it lie?
opts: 6 left of the origin and 2 up
6 right of the origin and 2 up
2 left of the origin and 6 up
2 right of the origin and 6 down
b.why: Written as −6 + 2i, the real part is −6 and the imaginary part is 2. So the point is (−6, 2): 6 left and 2 up. Taking the first number written (2) as the real part swaps the axes and gives the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Rewrite it as a + bi before reading off the parts.

b.best: 6 left of the origin and 2 up

final.title: The Argand plane
card: A complex number \(z = a + bi\) has a real part \(a\) and an imaginary part \(b\). Both \(a\) and \(b\) are ordinary real numbers.
The Argand plane shows complex numbers as points. The horizontal axis is the real axis. The vertical axis is the imaginary axis.
To plot \(z = a + bi\), go \(a\) units along the real axis and \(b\) units up the imaginary axis. This gives the point \((a, b)\).
Example: \(3 - 2i\) has real part 3 and imaginary part \(-2\). It is plotted at \((3, -2)\), which is 3 right and 2 down from the origin.

final.remember: Real part goes across, imaginary part goes up: \(a + bi\) is the point \((a, b)\).

a.q: At which point is the complex number \(-4 + 5i\) plotted on the Argand plane?
a.why: The real part \(-4\) gives the horizontal position and the imaginary part 5 gives the vertical position, so the point is \((-4, 5)\). \((5, -4)\) swaps the axes. The \(i\) is not part of the coordinate, because the imaginary part is the number 5.
a.clue: Real part first, then the number in front of \(i\).

b.q: Zara plots the complex number \(2i - 6\) on an Argand plane. Where does it lie?
opts: 6 left of the origin and 2 up
6 right of the origin and 2 up
2 left of the origin and 6 up

b.why: Written as \(-6 + 2i\), the real part is \(-6\) and the imaginary part is 2. So the point is \((-6, 2)\): 6 left and 2 up. Taking the first number written (2) as the real part swaps the axes and gives the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Rewrite it as \(a + bi\) before reading off the parts.
